Description

Do you want to help education technology companies build what's next with generative AI? Do you enjoy owning the technical relationship with a customer, from the first architecture whiteboard to a production launch at scale? Would you like a seat on a sales team where your technical judgment shapes the plan and the strategy?

Amazon Web Services is looking for a Senior Solutions Architect to join the EdTech team in the Worldwide Public Sector (WWPS) organization. You'll be the trusted technical advisor to a set of strategic EdTech customers, from fast-growing startups to established learning platforms that serve millions of students and teachers. You'll help them design, build, and scale on AWS, with a focus on bringing generative and agentic AI into their products in ways that are secure, cost-effective, and ready for production.

From idea to IPO and beyond, AWS sets the standard for education technology. The AWS Cloud lets EdTechs build and launch solutions that help students learn every day. You'll work on problems like scaling for back-to-school peaks, building AI tutors and assistants that teachers and districts can trust, protecting student data, and turning years of learning data into products that improve outcomes.

Key job responsibilities

Own the technical engagement for a portfolio of strategic EdTech customers, and be accountable for their architecture decisions and their success on AWS.
Lead generative AI engagements from use case to production, using services such as Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker AI, and Amazon Q, including RAG, agents, evaluation, and guardrails.
Design secure, scalable architectures that meet the privacy and compliance expectations of schools and districts.
Partner with account managers on account plans, and bring a technical point of view to strategy, opportunity reviews, and executive conversations.
Turn what you see across customers into reusable patterns, and bring customer feedback to AWS service teams to influence the roadmap.
Raise the bar for the SA community by mentoring other Solutions Architects, sharing best practices, and speaking at customer and industry events.
Travel up to 25 to 30% to meet with customers and partners.

Key job responsibilities

Execution of a strategic technical account plan for platform adoption (e.g., establish relationships to influence technical stakeholders);
Direct customer interaction to technically qualify and validate sales opportunities (e.g., conduct architecture meetings to validate solution);
Thought leadership engagements to evangelize and advocate for the AWS platform (e.g., public speaking at customer/partner events) ;
Curation and documentation of best practices to accelerate deployments of AWS solutions (e.g., public whitepapers, blogs, code);
Conducting technical enablement for customers/partners (e.g., Immersion Days); and
Capturing customer feedback and demand for evolving the AWS platform.

A day in the life

You might start with an architecture review for a customer launching an AI teaching assistant. Then you build a proof of concept on Amazon Bedrock, and end the day walking a CTO through a plan to cut inference cost before back-to-school. You'll go deep with engineers and stay strategic with executives, often on the same day.

About The Team

EdTech West is a subregion of the North America-based WWPS EdTech organization. The team covers eight territories, each containing multiple customer accounts. Every territory operates with a paired Solutions Architect (SA) and Account Manager (AM).

EdTech and its sister GovTech teams (collectively "xTech") belong to the State and Local Government and Education (SLG/EDU) domain.

Our Customers

EdTech customers are Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) that build and deliver SaaS products for education institutions. Most are private-equity backed commercial companies. They prioritize speed to market, cost control, and product innovation. A large portion of our engagements center on guiding these customers through on-premises-to-cloud migrations and Generative AI adoption.

Industry Rhythm

The education technology industry operates on a seasonal cycle aligned with the academic calendar. Customers deploy their largest application and workload changes during summer months when end-user disruption is lowest. New projects, regional expansions, and application launches occur throughout the year.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Inclusive Team Culture

Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Basic Qualifications

3+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
10+ years of IT development or implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries experience

Knowledge of AWS services, market segments, customer base and industry verticals
Experience working with end user or developer communities
Experience architecting infrastructure solutions using both Linux/Unix and Windows with specific recommendations on server, load balancing, HA/DR, & storage architectures
Experience communicating across technical and non-technical audiences, including executive level stakeholders or clients
Experience in SAP clean core design concepts, including design and build using non-SAP technologies in domains such as Generative / Agentic AI, and data & analytics

new_jobs.title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Radar
new_jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Radar ML team builds the machine learning systems that power Stripe’s Radar fraud and abuse product suite. Our models make real-time decisions across a significant share of internet commerce - helping businesses stop fraud, increase authorization, and grow safely. By turning economy-scale datasets into compelling ML products, the team directly improves customer outcomes and drives meaningful revenue for Stripe.

The team is growing, and expanding into multiple new areas. We are building abuse protections across the full customer life-cycle, adaptive and customizable fraud systems for enterprises, and risk intelligence for 50+ global payment methods.

What you’ll do

You will lead the machine learning strategy for abuse prevention across the full customer lifecycle. Abuse doesn't stop at the payment. Bad actors create fake and duplicate accounts, take over legitimate ones, farm free trials and promotions, resell access they obtained below cost, use services they never intend to pay for, and file bad-faith refunds and disputes. For AI companies, every abusive account burns real compute, and the same actors keep moving from one account, product, and access path to the next.

Stripe is uniquely positioned to solve this. Our network sees consumers across millions of businesses, so we can recognize a bad actor at signup, at login, at payment, and long after. Radar has already shipped the first building blocks: account evaluations at signup and login, customer-level abuse risk, and APIs that let businesses report their own abuse outcomes. You will turn these building blocks into a unified abuse prevention layer that understands the consumer behind every event and helps businesses act consistently across all of that consumer's accounts. This is a large growth opportunity for Radar, and a strategic priority for Stripe.

This is a fast-moving 0→1 area, built alongside some of the world's leading AI companies, and the attacks are real today. Labels are sparse, delayed, and differ by business. Much of the customer journey is only partly visible to us. Adversaries adapt as soon as we ship. You will set the technical direction, make the hard architecture calls, and personally build the hardest pieces.

Responsibilities

Set the technical strategy and multi-quarter roadmap for lifecycle abuse ML, with product and engineering leadership: which abuse vectors to take on, in what order, and with what approach.
Design a persistent, continuously updated consumer risk profile that combines signals from signups, logins, payments, product usage, refunds, and disputes. Evolve it from explainable composite scores toward model-driven risk scores for each type of abuse.
Lead development of models for abuse vectors such as multi-accounting, account takeover, bots, free-trial and promotion abuse, unauthorized resale, non-payment, refund abuse, and friendly fraud. Use graph, sequence, and LLM-based approaches over payment, account, and product-usage data.
Solve the label problem by designing ways to learn from sparse, delayed, merchant-specific, and weak labels, including merchant-shared feedback, LLM-assisted labeling, and network-level signals.
Define how we measure success: evaluation frameworks, impact and ROI estimates, and operating-point guidance that help businesses trade off abuse losses against growth and conversion.
Turn detection into action by shaping the risk controls, interventions, and recommendations businesses can turn on at each step of the customer journey.
Stay deeply hands-on: write substantial production code, prototype quickly, and personally land the most technically difficult components, with the reliability and latency standards of systems in Stripe's critical path.
Break ambiguous problems into parallel workstreams, unblock other engineers, and raise the team's bar through design review, code review, and mentorship.
Partner directly with leading Stripe users, fraud experts, product, and adjacent Stripe teams to ground the work in real user pain and change course quickly based on what you learn.
Build AI-native tooling, agents, and workflows that let the team investigate attacks and build and operate models dramatically faster.

Who you are

You are a hands-on technical leader who has built ML systems that matter, shipped them to production, and led others in doing the same. You thrive in ambiguity. You can take an open-ended problem with messy data and incomplete labels, find the highest-leverage path, get to user impact quickly, and change course when the data says so. You make the engineers around you better. You're as comfortable talking with a customer about the economics of their abuse problem as you are debugging a feature pipeline. You're excited to use frontier AI both in the systems you build and in how you build them.

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

10+ years of experience developing, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models in a production environment.
A track record of technically leading large, ambiguous ML initiatives from problem definition to production, with measurable business impact.
Deep expertise in machine learning, statistics, model evaluation, and experiment design, including where labels are noisy, delayed, or scarce.
Strong software-engineering skills, and you remain a hands-on contributor who regularly writes tested, maintainable production code.
Experience designing and operating production ML systems at scale, including data and feature pipelines, real-time inference, deployment, and monitoring, and making architecture tradeoffs across them.
Experience setting technical direction across multiple engineers or teams, and mentoring engineers to grow their scope.
Ability to explain complex tradeoffs clearly to engineers, product leaders, and customers, and to build alignment across functions.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience applying ML to fraud, abuse, integrity, trust and safety, identity, or security, where adversaries actively adapt to your defenses.
Experience with entity resolution, graph learning, or behavioral and sequence modeling of users, accounts, or devices (for example, detecting multi-accounting, account takeover, or bots).
Experience productionizing modern deep learning or LLM-based approaches, including using LLMs for labeling, investigation, or detection.
Experience building 0→1 ML products and working directly with customers to define what to build.
Experience building shared ML platforms, representations, or foundation models used across multiple products or teams.
Experience building AI-assisted tooling or agents that measurably increased a team's velocity.

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $253,500 - $380,300. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

new_jobs.description:
Senior Software Engineer - ML Infrastructure, Mobility Simulation and Planning

About The Role And Team

How can Uber plan pricing and incentives to meet financial goals while keeping its marketplace healthy and growing? That’s the challenge our Mobility Simulation and Planning (MSP) organization tackles within Marketplace.

MSP builds forecasting, simulation, and optimization products that help Operations teams translate financial targets into pricing and incentive policies across hundreds of cities. Our planning product, Planner, brings these capabilities together to generate actionable price plans. Supporting this work requires scalable model training and simulation, efficient distributed computing, and reliable workflows for generating and deploying plans.

The MSP Infra team
builds the data and computing foundations that make these capabilities possible. We partner with engineers, scientists, and shared-platform teams to turn complex modeling workflows into reliable, scalable, reusable infrastructure.

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer focused on ML infrastructure. You’ll build the frameworks, distributed execution capabilities, and developer tooling that help scientists develop, train, evaluate, and productionize models. Your work will make it easier to move from an experimental model to a dependable production workflow and to run the simulations and backtests needed to evaluate marketplace decisions.

How do we scale training and simulation across CPUs and GPUs? How do we make experiments reproducible and performance bottlenecks easy to diagnose? How do we support new modeling approaches without creating a separate infrastructure stack for every use case? You’ll solve these problems through hands-on engineering, close collaboration with modeling teams, and end-to-end ownership of production systems.

What You’ll Do

Build shared ML frameworks: Design and evolve reusable interfaces and libraries for model development, training, inference, evaluation, and backtesting.
Scale distributed workloads: Build and optimize execution capabilities for training, simulation, and optimization across CPU and GPU infrastructure.
Accelerate experimentation: Develop tooling for hyperparameter tuning, experiment tracking, reproducibility, and performance analysis so scientists can evaluate ideas faster.
Simplify productionization: Create reliable orchestration, configuration, dependency management, and deployment patterns that reduce the gap between experimentation and production.
Improve performance and efficiency: Profile workloads, diagnose compute and memory bottlenecks, and make thoughtful tradeoffs across runtime, resource utilization, reliability, and cost.
Build on shared platforms: Partner with Uber’s ML and compute platform teams to adopt and extend common capabilities rather than maintain isolated infrastructure.
Own systems and raise the engineering bar: Lead projects from design through rollout and operations, participate in on-call and incident response, and mentor engineers through design and code reviews.

Basic Qualifications

6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including work on ML infrastructure, distributed computing, or production platforms for computationally intensive workloads.
Strong programming skills in Python and experience building maintainable, well-tested software.
Experience designing, building, and operating distributed systems or workflow execution infrastructure.
Experience supporting production ML workflows, such as model training, batch inference, evaluation, or deployment.
Understanding of performance fundamentals, including parallelism, memory management, data movement, and resource utilization.
Experience delivering technical projects from design through production rollout and ongoing operations.
Ability to communicate technical tradeoffs and collaborate across engineering, data science, and platform teams.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Ray or comparable distributed computing frameworks.
Familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, PyTorch Lightning, or LightGBM.
Experience with distributed training, GPU performance profiling, or CPU/GPU workload optimization.
Experience building hyperparameter tuning, experiment tracking, or model evaluation infrastructure.
Experience supporting large-scale simulation, backtesting, forecasting, or optimization workloads.
Familiarity with workflow orchestration, containerized execution, CI/CD, and build or dependency-management systems.
Experience designing shared frameworks or developer platforms adopted by multiple modeling teams.
A track record of measurable improvements in training or inference performance, infrastructure reliability, compute efficiency, or model-development productivity.

new_jobs.description:
Cohesity is a leader in AI-powered data security and management. Aided by an extensive ecosystem of partners, Cohesity makes it easy to secure, protect, manage, and get value from data — across the data center, edge, and cloud. Cohesity helps organizations defend against cybersecurity threats with comprehensive data security and management capabilities, including immutable backup snapshots, AI-based threat detection, monitoring for malicious behavior, and rapid recovery at scale.

We’ve been named a Leader by multiple analyst firms and have been globally recognized for Innovation, Product Strength, and Simplicity in Design.

Join us on our mission to shape the future of our industry.

Research Engineer, Post-Training & Vision-Language Models

Want to join the leader in AI-powered document understanding?

About the Role
:

Enterprise documents such as contracts, invoices, filings and reports hold some of the world’s most valuable data, and most of it is still locked in layouts, tables and charts that software struggles to read. The Gaia team at Cohesity is building a world-class agentic document processing product to change that.

At its heart are vision language models (VLMs) that read documents as images, extract structured data, understand complex layouts, tables and charts, and answer questions about their content. We’re looking for a Research Engineer to push that capability forward.

You’ll work where research meets production, owning the fine-tuning, evaluation and data pipelines that determine how well our models understand and act on real enterprise data. You’ll have broad scope, significant compute, and a direct line from your work to a shipping product. The problems are open-ended: the path is ambiguous, the signal is noisy, and the right answer takes both research taste and engineering execution.

Cohesity is the leader in AI-powered data protection and security, trusted by over 13,600 enterprise customers, including more than 85 of the Fortune 100 and nearly 70% of the Global 500. Together they entrust us with over 200 exabytes of data. We’re backed by NVIDIA, IBM, HPE, Cisco, AWS, Google Cloud and others, and headquartered in Santa Clara, CA, with offices around the globe.

Want to join a scaled multi-billion ARR private company? On a team that’s operating like a Series A company?

HOW YOU'LL SPEND YOUR TIME HERE:

Evaluate, select, and adapt VLMs (open-weight and API-based) for document parsing, layout understanding, table and chart extraction, OCR-heavy content, and document question answering.
Fine-tune vision-language models using SFT and latest RL techniques such as RLHF / RLAIF / RLVR, GRPO or PPO-style RL for document understanding to hill climb towards the best document understanding in the industry.
Build reinforcement learning (RL) training platforms, design reward signals, and optimize model reasoning.
Build and maintain evaluation harnesses to measure model performance across capability and reliability dimensions.
Create pipelines for synthetic data generation to support training and evaluation.
Develop and refine post-training recipes that measurably improve production model quality.
Collaborate with the agentic engineering team so agents can perceive and act on visual inputs such as documents, screens, and diagrams.
Debug training instabilities, regressions, and unexpected model behavior; establish best practices for reproducible training and experiment tracking.

WE’D LOVE TO TALK TO YOU IF YOU HAVE MANY OF THE FOLLOWING:

Experience

5+ years of professional experience in machine learning engineering or research.
Hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, using RL techniques or evaluating large language or vision-language models.
Track record of taking models from experimentation to production.

Education

Master’s degree or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related field preferred.

Required Skills

Languages: Python
ML/AI: PyTorch (or JAX), Hugging Face ecosystem, supervised fine-tuning, VLMs/LLMs
Evaluation: building eval harnesses and benchmarks for model quality
Data: synthetic data generation, data curation pipelines

Preferred / Nice-to-Have Skills

Document AI experience: OCR, layout analysis, table and chart extraction
Visual grounding and region-level reasoning
Post-training and distillation for smaller or on-prem-deployable models
Publications or open-source contributions in post-training, alignment, or multimodal models
Prior experience in enterprise data protection, security, or infrastructure software

Expectations from the Role

Balance research exploration with engineering rigor and reliable delivery.
Work effectively across research and engineering and stay productive amid ambiguity and shifting priorities.
Communicate experimental results and tradeoffs clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Be hands-on: write and review production-quality code and run experiments regularly.

new_jobs.title: Data Scientist
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Workhelix is an enterprise SaaS company with a single goal: helping organizations get the most out of their AI investments.

Our people and software combine to give leaders answers to the three critical questions about the business value of AI:

Where are our top opportunities to create value with AI?
Are our current efforts actually delivering? What’s their ROI?
How can we accelerate and increase the benefits of our AI?

To find answers for each customer, Workhelix applies our unmatched expertise in economics, AI, and data science. We have pioneered a task-scoring method to identify top GenAI opportunities, ensuring clear, data-driven deployment strategies. Our ROI monitoring suite applies Nobel Prize-winning economics to provide accurate, ongoing insights into the impact of GenAI implementations. Renowned AI and Economics thinkers including Andrew Ng, and cofounders Andy McAfee and Erik Brynjolfsson stand proudly behind our mission.

We maintain a culture established on five key principles. For more information on our leadership principles, please visit the careers page of our website.

Role

Workhelix is looking for a Data Scientist to own the analytical engine behind Nucleus, our core product, reporting directly to the Head of Engineering.

That engine starts by taking in different customer data sources and reconciling them into a structured, unified model. From there it runs the analyses that identify where AI can create value and how a company's current practices line up against those opportunities. The output is specific, actionable guidance: what to do next, for which teams, and why.

You will own that work end to end. You will also extend it; customers arrive with questions our existing analyses don't answer, and part of the job is deciding when to adapt something we have and when to build something new.

This is a production engineering role as much as an analytical one. You are not building notebooks for someone else to productionize. You write the code that ships, runs in containers, calls external services, and executes in our cloud infrastructure. You work in parallel with our product engineers and forward-deployed engineers, in their codebases as well as yours.

It is also a force-multiplier role. A meaningful part of your impact will come from building internal tools and raising the analytical fluency of the whole company, so that strategists, engineers, and leadership can answer their own questions instead of queuing behind you.

You are the only data scientist, so you set the roadmap. You will gather needs from forward-deployed strategists and product engineers, spot the patterns showing up across customers, decide what matters most, and sequence the work. This is an individual contributor role today with a clear path to leading a team as it grows.

Key Responsibilities:

What You’ll Do

Own the analytical pipeline

Own the data mart and the ETL that unifies disparate customer systems into a single model our analyses can run against
Build and maintain the AI assessment: task decomposition, task-level AI acceleration scoring, and comparison against observed AI usage
Design new analyses, adapted or custom, to answer questions specific customers bring us

Ship it as product

Write production code in Python and SQL that runs as part of the product, not alongside it
Orchestrate analytical workloads in cloud infrastructure (containers, step functions, external APIs)
Contribute directly to our product and platform codebases

Turn analysis into decisions

Build the visualizations and narratives that make findings land with technical and executive audiences alike
Work with customer stakeholders and internal teams to make sure methods are understood, trusted, and acted on

Uplevel The Company

Build internal tools that let others run their own analyses and decide what those tools should be
Raise the analytical bar across the organization

Set direction

Translate needs from forward-deployed strategists and product engineers into a prioritized data science roadmap
Identify problems recurring across customers and decide what becomes core product versus custom work

What We Value

Willingness to own your work all the way into production on cloud infrastructure, including containerized and orchestrated workloads. Direct experience with AWS or equivalent is great; a track record of learning unfamiliar technical territory and getting it right is equally good
Strong data visualization and narrative skills; you can make a complex method legible to people who will never read the code
Comfort reading current academic literature and translating it into something that generates value in practice
Judgment about when the simple approach captures most of the value, and the discipline to ship it rather than overbuild
Thoughtful, self-aware use of AI in your own work: you move fast with it, you know where your own gaps are, and you own every decision it touches rather than deferring to it
Communication that earns trust with engineers, executives, and customer stakeholders. Prior client-facing experience is welcome but not required

What You Bring

5+ years in data science, applied research, or a closely related field, with a demonstrated record of work that changed what a business did; not just analyses that were interesting, but analyses that were acted on
Recognized as a go-to voice on method and rigor wherever you've worked: the person others bring hard analytical questions to, and who sets the standard for how that work gets done
Strong programmatic thinking: structure, abstraction, failure modes, and architectural tradeoffs applied comfortably in Python and SQL. We care less about syntax than about whether you reason well about how code should be built, which matters more, not less, when AI is writing some of it
Strong data modeling instincts and experience with modern transformation or semantic layer tooling (dbt, Looker, or similar)
Depth across machine learning and predictive analytics, NLP including text embeddings and inference, and clustering methods such as hierarchical clustering
Working knowledge of causal inference from observational data and quasi-experimental design

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days:

Understand the pipeline and data model end to end, how it works, where it's fragile, and why it was built the way it was
Explain what Workhelix does and why it matters without jargon, to a customer or a colleague
Meet the strategists and engineers who depend on this work and heard what customers are actually asking for
Run analytical work independently, including for customers whose data doesn't fit the existing shape
Have opinions about what's missing and where the method or the pipeline is weakest

By 60 days:

Made real contributions to the methods themselves, not just run the ones that exist
Something you built is in production and running against customer data
Shaping the data science roadmap and able to defend your priorities against competing asks
Comfortable fielding methodology questions from internal teams and from customer stakeholders
Know which recurring customer questions should become core product and which should stay custom

By 90 days:

Own the data science roadmap and the sequencing behind it
Other people can depend on what you've built, in product and internally
At least one piece of this work is legible enough that someone outside data science can answer their own question with it
Set the standard for analytical rigor at Workhelix, people bring you hard questions, and the answers hold up

Base salary range 184K - 222K + Equity + Health Benefits

What You’ll Get

Competitive compensation package and benefits.
Chance to learn and collaborate with some of the most famous researchers in the AI and digital economy space: Andrew Ng, Erik Brynjolfsson, Andy McAfee, and Daniel Rock.
The unique opportunity to help build a company, culture, and products from the ground up with a team that values healthy working practices.
A high-trust, high-autonomy work environment.

At Workhelix, we stand committed to ensuring an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available without any discrimination. We believe diversity is critical to our success. Selection for employment will solely be based on qualifications, merit, and business needs. We encourage all qualified individuals to apply!

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Where AI Meets Medicine: Build the Future of Drug Discovery in the Heart of Silicon Valley!

Making medicine that’s never been made means doing what’s never been done. If you’re an engineer, scientist, or builder who thrives on problems no one has solved before, this is your invitation, we want you on the team. We are ready to challenge the status quo and push medicine forward, all in the name of health. Are you up for the challenge? If so, join us!

About The Lilly And NVIDIA Partnership

Lilly and NVIDIA are launching a new AI co-innovation lab in the heart of Silicon Valley — an up-to-$1 billion, multi-year commitment to solve drug discovery’s toughest challenges. The lab brings Lilly scientists, technologists, chemists and biologists together with NVIDIA engineers under one roof. Together, we are building purpose-built foundation and frontier AI models trained on Lilly data at scale, tightening the feedback loop between automated wet labs and computational dry labs, designing the next generation of medicines for millions of patients across the globe.

Position Summary

We are rebuilding the Design-Make-Test-Analyze (DMTA) cycle by integrating agentic AI, cloud-based orchestration, and LIMS infrastructure to connect experimental readouts with the tools that accelerate laboratory science.

You will engineer the connective tissue between agentic AI and physical lab systems building practical integrations with robotic platforms, analytical instruments, and data pipelines. You will design agent workflows that reason over experimental data, trigger automated actions, and surface insights to scientists.

This is an on-site hands-on individual contributor role: you will prototype rapidly, productionize what works, and collaborate with chemists, biologists, and automation engineers to deploy intelligent systems that accelerate molecule discovery.

This position reports to the Agentic Automation Lead. You will own significant components of the agentic automation platform and be trusted to make technical decisions within them.

Key Responsibilities

Integration Engineering

Build and maintain the translation layer between high-level agent planning logic and low-level instrument control across lab automation platforms (Hamilton, Tecan, Opentrons) and analytical instruments (LC/MS, NMR, HPLC)

Connect experimental readouts to ELN/LIMS and downstream data pipelines so every run produces model-ready, traceable data

Agent Development

Build multi-agent systems with robust orchestration, state management, error recovery, and tool integration

Prototype and iterate rapidly on agent planning strategies, memory systems, and human-in-the-loop patterns

Solution Deployment

Partner with automation engineers and scientists to transition prototypes into reliable lab operations

Deploy and maintain containerized services using Docker and Kubernetes with GitOps and CI/CD practices

Integrate cloud-based orchestration frameworks such as Argo on Kubernetes with laboratory control systems

Collaboration & External Engagement

Work directly with NVIDIA engineers and researchers and with Lilly scientists in the co-innovation lab

Evaluate open-source projects, vendor tooling, and academic work for practical fit

What Success Looks Like

Autonomous agents reliably execute multi-step experiments on physical laboratory instruments

Measurable reduction in DMTA turnaround through autonomous planning and execution

Basic Qualifications

PhD (or MS + 3 yrs / BS + 5 yrs equivalent experience) in Chemical / Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Chemistry, or a related discipline, with demonstrated wet-lab automation experience

Direct experience integrating software control and/or AI systems with lab automation platforms (liquid handlers, analytical instruments, robotic workflows)

Preferred Qualifications

Strong experience with containerization (Docker) and Kubernetes-based orchestration in production environments

Experience building scalable, production-grade Python applications using tools such as Redis, FastAPI, Flask/Streamlit, and pytest (GitHub portfolio a plus)

A Forward Deployed Engineer II (FDE II) embeds directly inside a strategic enterprise customer to independently design, build, deploy, and run AI-powered production systems alongside the customer's engineering team. FDE IIs write production-grade software and own delivery of complete AI workstreams end-to-end — from requirements gathering through production deployment — combining the technical rigor of an AWS SDE with the urgency and ownership required to deliver measurable customer business outcomes.

FDE IIs are autonomous contributors. They deliver working features spanning the full software lifecycle. They design cohesive implementations for well-understood problems, making design trade-offs with appropriate guidance. They take on projects where the business problem is understood but implementations are not fully fleshed out, balancing constraints and limiting short-term workarounds. Key job responsibilities

Embed within customer engineering teams. Work with customers, stakeholders, and peers to understand the business and customer value of the systems you build. Understand the customer's business processes, technical architecture, and operational constraints. Build production AI applications. Design and develop production-grade software powering AI and agentic workflows — retrieval pipelines, workflow automation, API orchestration layers, data integration. Solve difficult problems with visible risks or roadblocks, bringing clarity and identifying simple designs for solutions. Integrate foundation models, customer data sources, and existing applications into cohesive AI experiences. Optimize for latency, reliability, and cost.
Own production for your workstream. Be a significant contributor to the full software development lifecycle including scoping, design, code, testing, deployment, and maintenance. new_jobs.title: E11 Bio - Machine Learning Scientist I/II
new_jobs.description:
E11 Bio is on a mission to advance connectomics towards the scale of whole mammalian brains. We are a collaborative and interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers engaged in a neuroscience moonshot project to develop a radical technology platform for scalable brain mapping. E11 Bio is a non-profit Convergent Research focused research organization located in Alameda, California, pursuing blue-skies neuroscience research yet operating like a nimble, tight-knit start-up. Read our technology roadmap .

We are seeking a creative and mission-driven Machine Learning Scientist to develop scalable automatic proofreading methods leveraging barcode and shape information. In this role, you will own core ML pipelines for automated proofreading of neuron and synaptic reconstructions in optical connectomics datasets, working closely with wet lab scientists, microscopists, and domain experts to ensure biological fidelity and scalability. Your work will directly support E11’s goal of making reliable connectomic data accessible to the broader neuroscience community.

In this role you will be focused on decreasing segmentation and proofreading costs for optical connectomics datasets that we are generating at E11, a critical bottleneck in the connectomics field. You will be responsible for improving initial segmentations using large spatial contexts with rich data features, and ingesting resulting datasets into scalable proofreading software for dissemination to the scientific community.

Responsibilities

Contribute to developing innovative ML approaches for automatic proofreading of segmentations in large PB-scale optical connectomics volumes, leveraging shape and barcode information
Own the deployment of scalable workflows to ingest large connectomic datasets into standard proofreading software (WebKnossos, CAVE)
Collaborate with academic and industry experts on building and extending tools for automated proofreading and interactive visualization
Develop, implement, and evaluate scalable pipelines for synapse detection and partner assignment in large-scale optical connectomics datasets, integrating morphological and protein labeling information
Identify and build ML-based image processing tools that remove key bottlenecks in our data processing and analysis pipeline
Maintain excellent laboratory science practices, communicate results through reports and presentations, and contribute to and assist in preparation of manuscripts, abstracts and other scientific documents.

Required Qualifications

Ph.D. in computer science, machine learning, applied math, computational biology or a related field in science and/or engineering or Ph.D.-equivalent publication history
3-5 years of relevant work or research experience, with strong history of independent and autonomous execution of novel ML solutions
Strong background in computer vision and applying ML tools to the analysis of large microscopy data sets
Experience with software engineering best practices (e.g. version control, code reviews, etc)
Excellent communication and collaboration skills, record keeping ability, and attention to detail

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with graph, sequence, or point based ML methods (GNNs, Transformers, Pointnets, etc.)
Experience with processing large chunked data (e.g Zarr) in the cloud (e.g. AWS or GCP)
Experience with large scale connectomics data and tools (e.g. Neuroglancer, WebKnossos, CAVE, CATMAID, etc.)
Strong record of publications in peer reviewed scientific journals a plus.

In The First Six Months, You Will

Become familiar with our existing ML and distributed processing code bases
Own the processing (segmentations) of a new dataset end-to-end and identify areas for improvement (accuracy and efficiency)
Integrate internal graph-based methods for automatic proofreading into standard block-wise workflows for PB-scale optical connectomics volumes
Optimize ingestion of smaller segmentation graphs into standard proofreading software (e.g WebKnossos, CAVE) for improving efficiency of ground truth generation

In 12 Months, You Will

Develop novel innovative ML approaches for automatic proofreading of neuron segmentations, leveraging both shape and barcode information
Contribute to algorithmic development across the segmentation pipelines increasing computational throughput
Contribute to achieving cubic-mm scale reconstruction at 100x lower proofreading costs
Scale ingestion of PB-sized optical volumes into proofreading software and pilot proofreading and dissemination of large connectomic subgraphs

You would love this job if…

You are passionate about moonshot neuroscience, and want to broadly accelerate science through long-term commitment to a high-impact project with a tight-knit team
You have a strong desire and intrinsic motivation to work collaboratively and inclusively as part of an interdisciplinary team science effort
You are committed to the ethos of open science, and want to see your work transparently disseminated
You’re mission-driven, and are seeking an environment where you can take long-term risks on moonshot science, shielded from academic or for-profit incentives
You’re seeking a high-leverage, non-traditional opportunity to maximize the impact of your science, establishing relationships with key stakeholders in the neuroscience community

We Offer

An opportunity to help change the world and work with a world-class interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers on a field-defining moonshot
Excellent medical, dental, and vision insurance through a PPO plan; parental leave.
Generous time off + paid holidays.

Stipend for fitness and wellness activities.

new_jobs.title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
new_jobs.description:
Position Overview

The Senior AI/ML Engineer designs, develops, deploys, and operates production-grade artificial intelligence and machine learning solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes. This role combines machine learning expertise, software engineering discipline, and solution architecture to translate complex business needs into secure, scalable, supportable, and responsible AI capabilities.

The Senior AI/ML Engineer provides technical leadership throughout the solution lifecycle, including discovery, architecture, data preparation, model development, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and continuous improvement. Working within a federated AI Center of Excellence (COE) model, this individual will partner with data engineering, analytics, product, architecture, cybersecurity, and business teams to develop and deliver business value through scalable AI and ML models.

Responsibilities

Model Development & Evaluation

Design, build, validate, and deploy machine learning models for complex business use cases.

Lead feature engineering, model selection, tuning, validation, and production-readiness assessments.

Select the simplest effective approach based on business requirements, data availability, explainability, operational constraints, and measurable performance.
Define model acceptance criteria and implement reproducible offline and production evaluations.
Assess model robustness, bias, explainability, limitations, and failure modes appropriate to the use case.

AI Solution Delivery & ML Operations

Own end-to-end delivery of AI/ML solutions from discovery and prototyping through production deployment and ongoing operation.
Implement model and data versioning, experiment tracking, reproducible pipelines, automated deployment, and rollback practices.
Establish monitoring for data quality, data drift, model performance, reliability, latency, utilization, and cost.
Define retraining, release, environment-promotion, and lifecycle-management approaches.
Provide production support, perform root-cause analysis, and drive corrective and preventive actions for operational issues.

Generative AI Solution Engineering

Design and operationalize generative AI solutions using fit-for-purpose techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation, prompt orchestration, tool integration, and structured output.
Implement appropriate guardrails, human oversight, content controls, and monitoring.
Evaluate foundation models and AI platforms against business, security, architecture, and governance requirements and standards.

Data & Analytics Engineering Alignment

Work with large-scale structured and unstructured data to support AI/ML development and evaluation.
Define data requirements and partner with data engineering teams to improve data quality, availability, lineage, and observability.
Develop AI/ML-specific data transformations and features while partnering with data engineers on shared, governed, production-grade pipelines.

new_jobs.description:
Archer
is collaborating with Air
to connect them with exceptional professionals for this role.

Company Description

Air is the leader in Enterprise Readiness. Our mission is to establish readiness as a real-time condition that is continuously achieved. Today, a dangerous Readiness Gap exists between what the front line needs and what is delivered. Our AI-native platform, Air Enterprise Readiness, aligns development, production, delivery, and sustainment into one coordinated execution system for government agencies and industrial suppliers. By revealing true capacity, exposing real constraints, coordinating resources, and executing at the speed of operational demands, the front line gets what it needs to succeed.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior Machine Learning Engineer to join our AI/ML team and build the infrastructure that powers the development, evaluation, deployment, and continuous improvement of our language models and AI systems.

As our AI capabilities expand, we need robust infrastructure for moving models from experimentation into production. This role will own critical parts of that lifecycle, including LLMOps, fine-tuning infrastructure, model evaluation, dataset pipelines, experiment management, model serving, and production observability.

In order to do this job well: This is an engineering-heavy ML role. You will build platforms and infrastructure that allow AI engineers and researchers to rapidly experiment with models, datasets, and training techniques while maintaining the reproducibility, scalability, and reliability required for production systems.

You will work across the full model lifecycle - from dataset creation and experimentation through training, evaluation, deployment, monitoring, and iteration.

This role is a full-time position located out of our office in Arlington, VA / Pittsburgh, PA / San Francisco, CA / Anywhere in the US.

This role may require up to 25% travel, including periodic travel to our Pittsburgh, PA and Arlington, VA offices for team collaboration, planning activities, and in-person meetings.

Scope of Responsibilities

Design and build LLMOps infrastructure supporting the development, evaluation, deployment, and continuous improvement of production language models.
Build scalable training and fine-tuning infrastructure for commercial and open-weight language models.
Develop pipelines supporting supervised fine-tuning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, preference optimization, and other post-training techniques.
Build infrastructure for distributed training and GPU-accelerated ML workloads.
Develop data pipelines for training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and synthetic data generation.
Build systems for dataset versioning, lineage, quality validation, transformation, and reproducible experimentation.
Develop experiment management infrastructure that enables engineers to compare models, datasets, hyperparameters, prompts, and training techniques.
Build automated evaluation pipelines that determine whether new models or model versions are ready for production deployment.
Design model registries, artifact management, versioning, and promotion workflows across development and production environments.
Build and operate scalable model-serving and inference infrastructure for open-weight and fine-tuned models.
Develop abstractions that allow product and AI engineering teams to use multiple models and inference providers without tightly coupling applications to a single model or vendor.
Build observability for model training and inference, including metrics, tracing, logging, resource utilization, model quality, latency, throughput, and cost.
Optimize training and inference workloads for GPU utilization, throughput, latency, reliability, and infrastructure cost.
Build automated workflows for model deployment, rollback, canarying, and production validation.
Investigate model and infrastructure failures across data pipelines, training jobs, inference services, distributed systems, and production environments.
Evaluate emerging models, training techniques, inference frameworks, and ML infrastructure and determine where they can improve our production systems.
Partner closely with AI engineers building agentic systems to provide the model, evaluation, and training infrastructure required to continuously improve those systems.

Qualifications

U.S. Citizenship is required

Required Skills

5+ years of experience building production machine learning systems, ML infrastructure, distributed systems, or similar technical systems.
Deep experience designing, building, and operating production ML infrastructure or ML platforms.
Experience building infrastructure for training, fine-tuning, evaluating, deploying, and monitoring large language models or other large-scale deep learning models.
Experience with LLM fine-tuning and post-training workflows, including techniques such as supervised fine-tuning, LoRA/QLoRA or other parameter-efficient approaches, and preference optimization.
Strong understanding of the modern LLM lifecycle, including data preparation, training, evaluation, model artifacts, deployment, inference, monitoring, and iteration.
Experience building reproducible ML pipelines involving dataset versioning, experiment tracking, model versioning, and automated evaluation.
Experience building and operating production GPU infrastructure across AWS, GCP, Azure, or dedicated GPU providers, including training and/or inference workloads.
Strong understanding of distributed systems and the challenges involved in running computationally intensive ML workloads at scale.
Strong programming experience in Python and experience building production-quality software.
Deep experience with containers, Kubernetes, and cloud platforms such as AWS, GCP, or Azure.
Experience designing scalable APIs, services, asynchronous workloads, and data-processing pipelines.
Strong understanding of observability and operational reliability for production ML systems.
Comfortable debugging failures across training code, datasets, models, GPUs, distributed systems, and cloud infrastructure.
Able to move between ML experimentation and infrastructure engineering, understanding the needs of researchers and AI engineers while building systems that make those workflows scalable and reproducible.
Comfortable working in a rapidly evolving field where tooling, models, and best practices change quickly.

Desired Skills

Current possession of a U.S. security clearance, or the ability to obtain one with our sponsorship
Experience in or exposure to the nuances of a startup or other entrepreneurial environment
Experience building secure code execution environments or sandboxes for AI agents.
Experience with multi-agent architectures, agent-to-agent communication, or distributed agent execution.
Experience with fine-tuning, post-training, reinforcement learning, or synthetic data generation.
Experience building AI observability, tracing, and debugging infrastructure.
Experience optimizing inference latency, throughput, GPU utilization, or model-serving costs.
Experience with AI security, adversarial testing, or securing agentic systems.
Experience working in government, defense, or other mission-critical environments.

We firmly believe that past performance is the best indicator of future performance. If you thrive while building solutions to complex problems, are a self-starter, and are passionate about making an impact in global security, we’re eager to hear from you.

new_jobs.description:
The Transportation Safety and Resilience Group develops integrated sensing and decision support systems that enable a safe and resilient global transportation system. We specialize in systems analysis, prototyping, system architectures, and algorithm development to support supply chain resilience, improving safety in the current airspace and the introduction of new and more autonomous vehicles into the existing transportation system. A current focus area of our work is the safe and efficient introduction of Advanced Air Mobility vehicles and other new entrants into the National Airspace System. The systems we work on help prevent aircraft accidents in the existing airspace and are extensible to a more autonomous future airspace. We are also focused on improving the resilience and effectiveness of the Department of War supply chain. With technical expertise in real-time software architecture, systems analysis, advanced supercomputing-enabled modeling and simulation, machine learning, and system integration, our research teams take new ideas for solving problems and develop them into working prototypes. We are currently working on detect-and-avoid systems for both crewed and uncrewed aircraft systems, safety systems to prevent runway incursions, and decision support systems.

Job Overview

MIT Lincoln Laboratory Technical Staff provide critical through expert multi-domain or new-domain innovative research supporting the Laboratory’s national security mission. They prototype state-of-the-art technology solutions and engage across the program lifecycle, leading projects or major/multiple technical workstreams in partnership with project, program and team/Group leaders. As a Technical Staff member, you will lead complex technical efforts requiring deep expertise, sound judgment, with the ability to successfully navigate technical complexity. Depending on the level, you will lead projects, major workstreams, complex programs, multi-program initiatives, or technical portfolios on extraordinary technology prototype efforts and creative new ideas and approaches that support critical mission needs. Depending on the level, you will translate broad Group strategy into clearly defined research or executional deliverables. Through integrating your deep technical expertise across disciplines, you consistently drive high-quality mission outcomes.

As a successful candidate, you will connect deep and diverse technical expertise with broader Laboratory objectives, perform independent research, develop creative approaches, and translate broad strategy into executable plans. You will work across or guide multidisciplinary teams through ambiguous trade-offs; helping develop and execute programs, creating briefings and reports, and often interfacing with sponsors. You effectively support sponsor, mission-partner, and Laboratory leadership’s needs through daily or weekly technical briefings, program documentation, proposals, and may conduct advanced capability road mapping and development. You will also guide and mentor Associate Technical Staff, Assistant Technical Staff, and other technical support personnel.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

We are looking for applicants with an interest and background in applied engineering, modeling and simulation and machine learning to develop algorithms and systems for autonomous and semi-autonomous vehicles. Additionally, we are looking for applicants to develop new advanced decision support systems as well as architectures and techniques for advancing and deploying semi-autonomous systems in the broader transportation domain. Example problem areas include algorithm development for collision avoidance logic, real-time contingency management, inter-vehicle coordination, and validation of decision support, surveillance, and tracking systems. Successful candidates will develop the skills to analyze the operational problems in detail and to develop deployable solutions, while extending our impact to other areas of the transportation domain. The candidate should be familiar with developing solutions using modern machine learning approaches such as reinforcement learning. Additional responsibilities include leading and developing applied research and development programs in the transportation domain, formulating new approaches to existing challenges and publishing results in conferences/journals. The Transportation Safety and Resilience Group supports a hybrid work environment.

Minimum Qualifications

Candidates will be considered for the appropriate level based on their education, experience, demonstrated technical expertise and breadth, leadership responsibilities, and the scale and complexity of programs or technical efforts they have led.

Level 5 – Technical Staff

Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline or other relevant technical field and typically 6+ years of relevant experience; or Master’s degree and typically 4+ years of relevant experience; or PhD and typically 0+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Diverse technical expertise with demonstrated ability to adapt that expertise to unfamiliar or emerging disciplines, systems, mission areas, or methods.
Established education, skills, and experience demonstrating the ability to apply significant technical judgment to broad challenges requiring integration across related systems or methods.
Demonstrated ability to lead projects or major workstreams and deliver complex technical outcomes.
Experience evaluating trade-offs, recommending paths forward, and adapting technical approaches to evolving project needs.
Demonstrated mentorship, collaboration, and ability to communicate recommendations, risks, and technical findings to varied audiences.
Experience contributing to technical reports, papers, presentations, proposals, or other formal technical deliverables.

Level 6 – Technical Staff

Bachelor’s degree in a STEM discipline or other relevant technical field and typically 8+ years of relevant experience; or Master’s degree and typically 6+ years of relevant experience; or PhD and typically 2+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Deep and diverse technical expertise with demonstrated ability to integrate knowledge across domains and establish direction in evolving systems or mission areas.
Established education, skills, and experience demonstrating the ability to incorporate technical judgment, program context, and stakeholder input to solve broad technical challenges.
Proven experience leading complex programs, significant program elements, or multi-team technical efforts.
Demonstrated ability to evaluate alternatives, manage technical ambiguity, and influence decisions across teams or stakeholder groups.
Strong record of mentorship, collaboration, technical communication, and contribution to team or Group capability development.
Experience contributing to proposals, publications, technical reports, presentations, or other materials that shape program direction or technical initiatives.

Additional Minimum Qualifications

PhD in engineering, physics, Mathematics, or computer science or similar field; in lieu of a PhD, a Master’s degree with four years of relevant experience will be considered.
Experience with state of the art machine learning approaches and architectures
Experience developing algorithms and architectures for advancement and deployment of autonomous systems
Experience with reinforcement learning
Publication record with conference and/or journal articles
Experience with algorithmic software development in Python
Ability to collaborate well as part of a team with good interpersonal skills
Ability to effectively distill and distribute concepts and results to a wide audience

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of the air or surface transportation domain
Experience developing algorithms and/or mathematical models in a simulation environment and/or deploying and testing on hardware
Experience with Natural Language Processing, Natural Language Understanding or Automatic Speech Recognition
Experience in other programming languages such as Python, C++, MATLAB, Julia, etc.
Publications in (air) transportation related conferences/journals
Experience leading a small team
Experience with distributed computing and scalable machine learning frameworks

Experience submitting research proposals

Are you looking to power the next leap in the exciting world of advanced electronics?
Do you want to help solve problems that drive success in the rapidly evolving technology and connectivity landscape? Then bring your problem-solving, passion, and creativity to help us power the next leap in electronics.

At Qnity
, we’re more than a global leader in materials and solutions for advanced electronics and high-tech industries – we’re a tight-knit team that is motivated by new possibilities, and always up for a challenge. All our dedicated teams contribute to making cutting-edge technology possible. We value forward-thinking challengers, boundary-pushers, and diverse perspectives across all our departments, because we know we play a critical role in the world enabling faster progress for all. Learn how you can start or jumpstart your career with us.

Qnity is accepting applications for a full-time Senior AI Engineer position at one of Qnity’s main campuses in Wilmington, Delaware. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced artificial intelligence and backend software engineering professional to join a growing team that plays a vital and dynamic role in the company.

Qnity is a market leader in specialty materials for electronic devices and microchip fabrication. In this role, the Senior AI Engineer will collaborate with business, engineering, cloud platform, data engineering, and digital technology teams to architect, develop, integrate, deploy, and operate enterprise artificial intelligence platforms and backend systems.

AI and software engineering are integral to Qnity’s digital transformation, with opportunities for senior-level contributions in:

Enterprise AI platforms, agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and application integration
Python and FastAPI backend services, APIs, and data pipelines
Machine learning, deep learning, and computer vision solutions

The successful candidate will have experience delivering secure, production-grade AI applications and translating business requirements into reusable architectures, backend services, APIs, data pipelines, and cloud solutions. The role combines generative and agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation, deep learning, computer vision, and backend software engineering. The candidate will provide technical leadership across design, development, testing, deployment, monitoring, security, performance, and continuous improvement.

Architect and maintain AI platforms and backend services using Python, FastAPI, microservices, REST APIs, asynchronous processing, and secure integration patterns.
Define and implement the architecture for Qnity’s enterprise agentic AI platform using Microsoft Foundry, Azure AI Agent Service, and Microsoft Agent Framework, with reusable service, orchestration, security, and governance patterns.
Design, build, deploy, and support generative AI agents and retrieval-augmented generation solutions for enterprise knowledge use cases, integrating structured and unstructured data through semantic, vector, hybrid, metadata-filtered, and permission-aware search.
Develop computer vision and deep learning applications for image and video analysis, including object detection, tracking, feature extraction, anomaly detection, and model evaluation.
Implement identity, access control, secrets management, automated testing, deployment automation, logging, monitoring, performance, and reliability controls using Microsoft Azure cloud engineering and security practices.
Partner with business, scientific, software, data engineering, information security, and cloud teams to define requirements, prototype solutions, resolve integration and production issues, document architectures and APIs, and guide technical delivery.

Strong knowledge of AI system design, agent orchestration, machine learning, natural language processing, software architecture, API design, distributed systems, cloud security, CI/CD, observability, performance optimization, production reliability, and cross-functional technical communication.
Experience with Microsoft Azure technologies, including Azure OpenAI, AI Search, Function Apps, App Service, Blob/Data Lake Storage, Key Vault, Application Insights, Entra ID, RBAC, and managed identities.

Strong Copilot and agent extensibility experience with Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Copilot/Teams agents, MCP servers, custom connectors, function-calling tools, Adaptive Cards, Graph connectors, and governed enterprise integrations.
Advanced Python and SQL skills, with experience in FastAPI, microservices, REST APIs, asynchronous applications, data validation, automated testing, and enterprise integrations.
Hands-on experience designing and deploying generative AI, agentic AI, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), enterprise search, and Copilot or agent extensibility solutions using modern AI platforms, frameworks, model services, and tool-integration patterns.
Hands-on experience with computer vision and deep learning using PyTorch or TensorFlow, YOLO, OpenCV, convolutional neural networks, object detection, tracking, image or video processing, and model evaluation.
Experience with CI/CD, automated testing, source control, observability, application security, performance optimization, and production support using Azure DevOps or GitHub.

A&M is different by design: we give people ownership and impact from day one, fuel development through real opportunity, and provide direct access to leaders who invest in our growth. Guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity, our collaborative, globally minded environment is why our people love working at A&M.

A&M is seeking a Senior Associate to join A&M IQx, our AI-focused business unit. We design, build, and deploy AI solutions that help clients eliminate manual work, move faster, and deliver measurable results across industries.

Senior Software Engineer - ML Infrastructure, Mobility Simulation and Planning

About The Role And Team

How can Uber plan pricing and incentives to meet financial goals while keeping its marketplace healthy and growing? That’s the challenge our Mobility Simulation and Planning (MSP) organization tackles within Marketplace.

MSP builds forecasting, simulation, and optimization products that help Operations teams translate financial targets into pricing and incentive policies across hundreds of cities. Our planning product, Planner, brings these capabilities together to generate actionable price plans. Supporting this work requires scalable model training and simulation, efficient distributed computing, and reliable workflows for generating and deploying plans.

The MSP Infra team
builds the data and computing foundations that make these capabilities possible. We partner with engineers, scientists, and shared-platform teams to turn complex modeling workflows into reliable, scalable, reusable infrastructure.

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer focused on ML infrastructure. You’ll build the frameworks, distributed execution capabilities, and developer tooling that help scientists develop, train, evaluate, and productionize models. Your work will make it easier to move from an experimental model to a dependable production workflow and to run the simulations and backtests needed to evaluate marketplace decisions.

How do we scale training and simulation across CPUs and GPUs? How do we make experiments reproducible and performance bottlenecks easy to diagnose? How do we support new modeling approaches without creating a separate infrastructure stack for every use case? You’ll solve these problems through hands-on engineering, close collaboration with modeling teams, and end-to-end ownership of production systems.

What You’ll Do

Build shared ML frameworks: Design and evolve reusable interfaces and libraries for model development, training, inference, evaluation, and backtesting.
Scale distributed workloads: Build and optimize execution capabilities for training, simulation, and optimization across CPU and GPU infrastructure.
Accelerate experimentation: Develop tooling for hyperparameter tuning, experiment tracking, reproducibility, and performance analysis so scientists can evaluate ideas faster.
Simplify productionization: Create reliable orchestration, configuration, dependency management, and deployment patterns that reduce the gap between experimentation and production.
Improve performance and efficiency: Profile workloads, diagnose compute and memory bottlenecks, and make thoughtful tradeoffs across runtime, resource utilization, reliability, and cost.
Build on shared platforms: Partner with Uber’s ML and compute platform teams to adopt and extend common capabilities rather than maintain isolated infrastructure.
Own systems and raise the engineering bar: Lead projects from design through rollout and operations, participate in on-call and incident response, and mentor engineers through design and code reviews.

Basic Qualifications

6+ years of professional software engineering experience, including work on ML infrastructure, distributed computing, or production platforms for computationally intensive workloads.
Strong programming skills in Python and experience building maintainable, well-tested software.
Experience designing, building, and operating distributed systems or workflow execution infrastructure.
Experience supporting production ML workflows, such as model training, batch inference, evaluation, or deployment.
Understanding of performance fundamentals, including parallelism, memory management, data movement, and resource utilization.
Experience delivering technical projects from design through production rollout and ongoing operations.
Ability to communicate technical tradeoffs and collaborate across engineering, data science, and platform teams.
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Ray or comparable distributed computing frameworks.
Familiarity with ML frameworks such as PyTorch, PyTorch Lightning, or LightGBM.
Experience with distributed training, GPU performance profiling, or CPU/GPU workload optimization.
Experience building hyperparameter tuning, experiment tracking, or model evaluation infrastructure.
Experience supporting large-scale simulation, backtesting, forecasting, or optimization workloads.
Familiarity with workflow orchestration, containerized execution, CI/CD, and build or dependency-management systems.
Experience designing shared frameworks or developer platforms adopted by multiple modeling teams.
A track record of measurable improvements in training or inference performance, infrastructure reliability, compute efficiency, or model-development productivity.

Team:

Ilir Osmanaj, VP of AI Engineering Location:
